summary: 33-year-old at 22 weeks of pregnancy with a persistent firm lump and an axillary node, told it is "pregnancy changes". Pregnancy-associated breast cancer is diagnosed late: ultrasound and core biopsy are safe in pregnancy and must not be deferred; tamoxifen is contraindicated in pregnancy.

inputs.chiefComplaint: New lump in the left breast during pregnancy
inputs.hpi: Twenty-two weeks pregnant with her second child. Noticed a firm lump in the left breast 3 weeks ago that has not gone away; midwife said it is probably "pregnancy changes". Painless. Sister diagnosed with breast cancer at 41.

exam.other: Breasts: engorged pregnant breasts. 2.5 cm firm, ill-defined lump at 1 o'clock left breast, not tethered. No nipple change. Small firm left axillary node.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Persistent left breast lump in pregnancy (22 weeks) — exclude pregnancy-associated breast cancer
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Persistent breast lump (left) at 22 weeks of pregnancy with an axillary node — must exclude pregnancy-associated breast cancer. Ultrasound breast and axilla and core biopsy now; do not defer until after delivery.

mustExclude.note: Tamoxifen is teratogenic; it must not be proposed during pregnancy.

guideline.name: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 12 — Pregnancy and breast cancer
guideline.section: Diagnosis of a breast lump in pregnancy (ultrasound, core biopsy; delay in diagnosis); treatment during pregnancy (tamoxifen contraindicated)
guideline.citation: Royal College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists. Pregnancy and Breast Cancer. Green-top Guideline No. 12. London: RCOG; 2011.

guideline.name: NCCN Guidelines — Breast Cancer (inflammatory breast cancer; breast cancer during pregnancy)
guideline.section: Inflammatory breast cancer: core biopsy of breast and skin, staging, neoadjuvant systemic therapy before modified radical mastectomy (breast conservation and sentinel node biopsy not recommended); breast cancer during pregnancy (no tamoxifen, no radiotherapy during pregnancy)
guideline.citation: National Comprehensive Cancer Network. NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology: Breast Cancer (current version at authoring).

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — Suspected cancer: recognition and referral
guideline.section: Site-specific recommendations: breast cancer (age ≥30 unexplained lump; ≥50 unilateral nipple discharge/retraction; skin changes; men ≥50 subareolar mass), haematological cancers (unexplained lymphadenopathy), head and neck (unexplained thyroid lump)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected cancer: recognition and referral. NICE guideline NG12. London: NICE; 2015 (updated).

rationale: Permutation: pregnancy. Tests pregnancy-aware work-up (ultrasound, biopsy not deferred) and that pregnancy-contraindicated drugs are not proposed. Web receives pregnancy through pregnancyPossible; iOS only through free text.
